channel.title: Help: Questions Desk (new posts)
channel.description: Posts in the forum category "Help: Questions Desk" - If you've got questions about the sandbox, chat, formatting (wiki syntax/coding), or anything that involves the writing process and/or something you're currently writing, post here.

item.title: My first SCP article: Re: My first SCP article
item.content:encoded:
Okay maybe you need a history lesson. The term "Scapegoat" actually comes from the Bible, and this is real, you can look it up, Leviticus Chapter 16. In addition to the Ten Commandments given in the book of Exodus, the book of Leviticus lists a number of other laws for the nation of Israel and if a Jew breaks any one of those laws, that is a sin. The list is so exhaustive it's pretty much impossible for anyone to go long without committing one sin so they had a ritual to cleanse people of their sins by confessing to the High Priests from the line of Aaron and once a year they in turn would recite these sins over the head of a goat which they then allowed to escape into the wilderness of the desert and take those sins with them to the angel Azazel. Yes, this is a legit thing, and we still use that word to this day because of this ancient tradition.

So anyway, I figure if you put all the sins of an entire nation for a year on one poor little goat, that may have a sinister effect and maybe there's a herd of a few thousand immortal demon goats somewhere in the desert of Israel. It's actually an idea I had for a long time before I even came to this wiki. Actually all of them are, except that last SPC, but these ones I listed are ideas I had with no context and the SCP format looks like a good place to share them, just give you all an idea of what they are and what we're doing to keep them from killing us. Scapegoats and Swine Legion would actually fit well in the Competitive Eschatology Canon.

item.title: My first SCP article: Re: My first SCP article
item.content:encoded:
You should pick the idea that you're most excited about, frankly — or at least, most easily able to translate your excitement into words to aid the greenlight process.

Scapegoats - the cursed goats that carry the sins of the nation of Israel according to an ancient ritual.

Question, though, what are the "sins of the nation of Israel"?

item.title: My first SCP article: My first SCP article
item.content:encoded:
I am new and I have been thinking of a few ideas for SCP articles, but now that I have my big shot I don't which one you guys want to see first, so before I head in for the greenlight, does anyone wanna weigh in on which one you want to read that I should pitch first?

Playing with Fire - silly putty like substance that is plasma at room temperature, from Dr. Wondertainment.
Vampire Bodega - mini-mart where everything seems to be free, but actually draws blood from customers, not noticeable unless the customer comes more than twice a week. May be part of Marshall, Carter and Dark.
Cryovampire - cryogenically preserved person who was successfully revived, but now absorbs heat energy. Must be kept in a room heated to 98.6 degrees Farenheit at which point the ambient temperature neutralizes the anomaly, but as soon as it is exposed to lower temperatures it reverts to a savage that freezes anything it touches.
Alzoidian - a cephalopod like alien life form native to the red spot of Jupiter. Exists in symbiosis with a fungus and another species that resembles a manta ray. Still not quite sure how to explain how the foundation even acquired it…
Scapegoats - the cursed goats that carry the sins of the nation of Israel according to an ancient ritual.
Swine Legion - the cursed swine possessed by demons exorcised by Jesus.

SPC-2806: cybernetics for pugilists who lost limbs in shark attacks so that they may once again punch sharks.

item.title: Edit SCP or new tale?: Re: Edit SCP or new tale?
item.content:encoded:
I have an idea for an original character based around SCP-2806, should I edit the existing article to include him as a new instance

Since SCP-2806 is not tagged with "collaboration", you are not allowed to edit in new content without authorial permission. The SCP wiki's editing policy is noted in the required reading.

Should I do all that, or just post the interview as it's own tale with a reference to the article?

The latter. If you make an unauthorized edit to a page that you did not write, staff will revert the change.

item.title: Edit SCP or new tale?: Edit SCP or new tale?
item.content:encoded:
I have an idea for a character that I have a lot of confidence in, but I want to make sure I introduce him correctly. First impressions matter, and if I do this wrong, it could be the end for him, and maybe me too.

So the idea is a cyborg, but not really a complex cyborg, actually he just has a cybernetic arm. It's a concept I have worked with a lot, and I feel it could work with SCP-2806. I know I could make up something more original, but that entry felt like it had everything I needed to work with and I want to work with the universe rather than forcing it around me. The long term story is that he ends up in Alpha-9, but not because he's the coolest guy in the room, but because he got into a situation where he got the offer and it was either this or amnestics, and frankly it was enough on the edge the Foundation was cool either way. So the interesting part of the story is that this a guy who's saving the world one skip at a time because he was in the wrong place at the wrong time.

Where I'm at I think it would work to edit the original article adding the new instance to the description, adding a new containment procedure for the new instance, and an interview between the agent and the SCP to get some info on what seperated this guy from all the others that just get the Skywalker protocol. Should I do all that, or just post the interview as it's own tale with a reference to the article?

item.title: Creative Commons Limits: Licensing Staff Post
item.content:encoded:
A good thing to keep in mind is how easily you can swap this out with a similar brand/song, and retain a cohesive article. Say you write an SCP loosely surrounding "Hit Me With Your Best Shot." If you can swap that song out with "God Save the Queen," and not have any significant impact on your article, that is considered acceptable. Likewise, if your narrative involves a Macy's but can be replaced with a 99 cent store, that is acceptable as well.

Bear in mind if you do end up referencing a song, it's better to err on the safe side and just note who wrote the song in your author post. If you intend on using song lyrics, however, the situation becomes significantly more complicated and you will have to do your own research on whether the lyrics are still copyrighted or not.

item.title: Brainstorming - Amber Water: Re: Brainstorming - Amber Water
item.content:encoded:
Porting PM conversation:

+ show block
– hide block

I do have an alternate idea involving an amber mist that transports beings to an oceanic "gateway" world. There, I was thinking of exploring an SCP agent interacting with a cetacean and insectoid, both of whom were also transported to the world. It'd be more of an exploration of power dynamics and territorial advantage between sapient species. Do you think that'd have a better chance than this?

It depends. Some reviewers might ask why you're not writing a tale instead, especially if the core anomaly is material that exists in various forms on the site already.

Largely because the SCP in question does lead to a unique world, which requires its own SCP article. Plus, the SCP itself has some unique properties beyond just transporting a person to another place. I was thinking it could also be fairly nutritious, which is a key reason why the SCP agent in the story I plan to tell doesn't die of scurvy or malnutrition after being at sea for so long.

If it's meant to be primordial, it seems odd that the seaweed would be so conveniently well adapted to a modern human's digestive system. I feel like a different narrative approach would be needed. Timespace oddities and whatnot might even make more sense here from a story standpoint.

Hm. The question is how to do that inside of four hundred words. Would it help if I mentioned it was meant to be in journal format? I know that's been done several times, but… looking over the SCP's, some of my favorite stories have been journal-like narratives, and I think it'd work well in this case.

Could you elaborate a bit? Like, suggesting that this takes place in a past era of Earth? Or that time moves differently in this world, and hunger becomes a non-issue? If it's the latter, I did have an idea about time moving differently on this alien world, so that could inform him returning and noticing that little time has passed.

For the new discussion, I feel like the core narrative needs to be better established before you start thinking about mechanics. What is the backstory behind the world's existence and why are random trespassers not immediately ejected? If we know why the world behaves the way it does, we can better advise on how to make the mist effect match.

item.title: Brainstorming - Amber Water: Brainstorming - Amber Water
item.content:encoded:
Basically a brainstorming thread for a potential SCP.

The idea behind it involves an SCP that, in its present state at the time of the article, is a tank of amber-colored water. In a solid or liquid state, the water has no special properties other than its unusual color. In a gaseous state, however - particularly a semi-gaseous mist - the water transports whomever travels through it to an oceanic world with no fauna.

Despite this, I'm thinking that the world is very friendly to life - the seas are freshwater, and there's a diverse ecosystem of plant life beneath the surface, some of which are edible and moderately nutritious to humans, despite their alien nature.

The SCP story itself involves an SCP scientist who's sent to investigate the unusual amber cloud hovering about a mile off the coast of Tanzania, when a powerful wind blows it into him before he has time to adjust his course, transporting him to the oceanic world, where he encounters a large sentient cetacean-like creature and a sentient, flying arachnid-like creature. The story itself would explore the backstory of the world, and the interactions of three sentient creatures and how they interact with their environment when they're unequally built for it, and the power dynamic that emerges as a result of their unequal adaptations.

I'm still figuring out the mechanics behind the mist itself, though the fact that it only facilitates transportation as a mist and not in any other state of matter is key to the story's resolution.

item.title: Getting Sandbox Feedback without Greenlight?: Re: Getting Sandbox Feedback without Greenlight?
item.content:encoded:
Agreeing with Hexick's post above, and noting that if you're looking to work on your writing skills specific to SCP articles, you don't necessarily need to ask for feedback on a whole draft. If you're seeking to improve clinical tone, for example, you can post short excerpts in the Questions Desk forum to ask for opinions on what to improve. You can also ask for tips on writing certain parts of an SCP article, such as interviews. Examples of such threads include:

  • http://scp-wiki.wikidot.com/forum/t-13834538/dialogue-and-interviews
  • http://scp-wiki.wikidot.com/forum/t-13787438/references-for-ideas-on-interactions-between-foundation-and
  • http://scp-wiki.wikidot.com/forum/t-13696555/containment-procedure-required
  • http://scp-wiki.wikidot.com/forum/t-13695935/how-much-is-too-much-detail

Oftentimes a draft isn't interesting to a reviewer because the core concept is boring/unwieldy. If you're going to ask someone to review an entire sandbox draft, ideally you'd have an interesting concept written up and not just a throwaway practice premise that might introduce issues that will distract a reviewer from focusing on the writing separate from the concept.

item.title: I made my first scp!: Forum Crit Team - Staff Post
item.content:encoded:
Hey Dreswrites: this is not the place for this. If you want to announce a SCP, you should use the announcements thread: http://www.scpwiki.com/forum/t-13597458/scp-announcements-46:aristotle-axolotl-throttle; or mention it in #site19 on IRC.

If you're looking for feedback on the SCP, I would direct you towards either #thecritters on IRC, or to the required reading for this forum: http://www.scpwiki.com/forum/t-13282684/required-reading:how-to-use-this-forum-ideas if you're wanting feedback on the idea as a whole. If you want feedback on the concept, you can edit this post (using the 'Edit' button under the blue 'Options' in the bottom right corner of the post, not the red 'Edit' at the bottom of the page) to use the required format.

Alternatively, the Swamp Critter Roster lists people who will give feedback on posted works.

item.title: Getting Sandbox Feedback without Greenlight?: Re: Getting Sandbox Feedback without Greenlight?
item.content:encoded:
Greenlights, while highly recommended for first-time authors, are only required to post in the Draft Critique Forum, and are obtained via concept threads in the Ideas Forum.

Additionally, another way of receiving critique is through the #thecritters chatroom on our IRC network (SkipIRC | irc.scpwiki.com | SSL Port: 6697), which while it doesn't require greenlights to get feedback there, some reviewers may refuse to look at drafts for new writers who haven't already gotten greenlights in the forums. If you want to head over there, make sure to read the Chat Guide I previously linked, and either way, I strongly recommend you go through the greenlight process in addition.
